html:
Babylon was an ancient city on the Euphrates in southern Mesopotamia, about 85 kilometres south of modern Baghdad in Iraq. For over a thousand years it was the chief city of Babylonia, and at times the largest city in the world.

It was a minor town until Hammurabi, in the 1700s BCE, made it the capital of the Old Babylonian kingdom, which ruled all of southern Mesopotamia. His law code is the best known from the ancient world. The Hittites sacked the city around 1595 BCE. Kassite kings then ruled it for centuries, and Babylon stayed the religious and learned heart of the land, the home of its god Marduk, even under Assyrian rule.

Its greatest days came under the Neo-Babylonian Empire in the 600s and 500s BCE. Nebuchadnezzar II rebuilt it with huge walls, the blue-glazed Ishtar Gate, a processional way and a great ziggurat, likely the source of the story of the Tower of Babel. He also destroyed Jerusalem in 587 or 586 BCE and took many Judeans into exile in Babylon. The Hanging Gardens are said to have been here, but no trace has been found.

In 539 BCE Cyrus the Great took Babylon without a long fight, and it became a capital of the Persian Empire. Alexander the Great died in Nebuchadnezzar's palace in 323 BCE. After his successors built Seleucia nearby, Babylon slowly emptied. Its ruins were dug up in the early 1900s.
sum: Babylon was an ancient city on the Euphrates in southern Mesopotamia, about 85 kilometres south of modern Baghdad in Iraq. For over a thousand years it was the chief city of Babylonia, and at times the largest city in the world.
